- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca573188e0ea75500eaf05a84dd5dea92cecaf24` — the merge of head `5318e581015920941957e2650d6115310041011d` into base `973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca573188e0ea75500eaf05a84dd5dea92cecaf24 && git checkout ca573188e0ea75500eaf05a84dd5dea92cecaf24
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703 5318e581015920941957e2650d6115310041011d && git checkout -B drift-repro 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703 && git merge --no-ff 5318e581015920941957e2650d6115310041011d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5318e581015920941957e2650d6115310041011d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (the grants bridge), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`FlowUserGrants`, `resolveRunContext`, `seedRunGrants`, `resolveDecisionSegmentContext`, `runUserOf`), packages/services/service-automation/src/runtime-identity.ts (`RunIdentityContext`, `resolveRunDataContext`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/rls-compiler.ts (the `current_user.email` binding, read only), packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (`resolveUserAuthzGrants` and the request path, read only), packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts `buildAutomationContext` and packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts `dispatchFlowAction` (the two doors, read only), packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts (the record-change envelope, read only), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/subflow-node.ts and map-node.ts (child contexts, read only), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts `SEED_USER_GRANTS` (read only), the changeset and the four test files of the diff.

Read at 2026-10-19T19:29Z on PR #24636's head: card #24613 (its body, triage 6272563947, claim 6272823429 and the os-dev-report 6274876489), the PR body and its one comment (the advisory docs-drift check), the net diff against merge base `973917c5795f7a440d46a15bc5cf8961af9d8703` (9 files, +527 −41; the merge of `main` the head carries is not judged), and every check-run on the head, re-read after the last one completed. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally; the ablation and before-leg readings below are the dev's, cited as reported.

### ① Derived judgments

**D1 — a `runAs:'user'` run now reaches exactly the rows its user's own request reaches, and nothing beyond: RIGHT.** The email a run carries has exactly two sources. (a) The core resolver: `plugin.ts` bridges `setUserGrantsResolver` to `resolveUserAuthzGrants(ql, userId, { tenantId, bypassGrantsCache: true })` and now spreads `grants.email` when present; core fills `grants.email` from the `sys_user` row of that same `userId` (the `getUserRow` fallback) — the stored email of the run's own user, never a different user's. (b) A context that already carries one is kept verbatim (`needsEmail = !runContext.email`). Who can supply (b): the REST trigger door `buildAutomationContext` builds the context from named fields only and routes unknown body keys into `params`, so no request body key can land on `email`; the action door `dispatchFlowAction` lists its fields explicitly and forwards no email; the record-change trigger hands `record`, `previous`, `object`, `event`, `userId`, `tenantId` and `params` only; a `subflow` / `map` child spreads its parent's context (the same user's run); a resumed leg carries the run's own persisted context. No public door lets a caller write someone else's email; the in-process `execute(name, context)` is a service API whose caller already controls `userId`, `positions` and `permissions`, a trust boundary this diff does not move. On the consuming side the RLS compiler binds `current_user.email` from the execution context's `email` and nothing else (`rls-compiler.ts`, the `userCtx` build), and `resolveRunDataContext`'s user arm copies `context.email` only when present and invents nothing. Direction: with the email the run's envelope is still a subset of the request's (`accessible_org_ids`, `systemPermissions` remain absent on the run — pre-existing, outside this card, and narrowing); without it, every email-keyed policy drops out, narrowing again. The real-stack pin `runas-user-email-owner.integration.test.ts` holds the control, the guard, the card's reproduction, the doors' forwarded shape and the "someone else's email is still refused" case. One difference to name: the request path keeps a session email over the stored one, while no door forwards the session email and the run always takes the stored one. The two coincide for a `sys_user` whose session and stored email agree, which is how the auth plugin keeps them; a divergence makes the run different-or-narrower, never wider. The dev noted it unfiled; I agree.

**D2 — the decider's segment (PR #24527's path): RIGHT.** `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` now deletes `switched.email` beside `positions`, `permissions` and `org_user_ids`, and does so before the `runAs === 'system'` early return, so the submitter's email leaves the context on both postures. On the user posture `seedRunGrants(run.flowName, switched, 'deciding')` sees `needsEmail` true and resolves the decider's own stored email through the same resolver. Without the removal the decider would run under the submitter's email, which the dev's second ablation reports as a real-stack leak (the decider wrote the submitter's row). Pinned at the envelope layer (`resume-decider-identity.integration.test.ts`: the decider's email after a decision, the submitter's email before it, the failed-resolution case answering undefined, and both `runAs:'system'` decision cases carrying no email) and on the real stack (the decider's row stamped with the decider; the submitter's row refused to the decider as the decider's own request is).

**D3 — the `runAs:'system'` arm is unchanged: RIGHT.** The only line the diff adds to `resolveRunDataContext` is `if (context.email) out.email = context.email;` in the user arm, after the fail-closed `userId` check; the system arm's envelope (`isSystem: true`, `actor`, optional `userId` / `tenantId`, empty `positions` / `permissions`, optional `flowRunId`) is byte-identical to the base, and `seedRunGrants` still resolves nothing when `runContext.runAs === 'system'`. Pinned in `crud-runas.test.ts` (`'email' in c.ctx` is false on a system run) and by the real-stack system control. The claim's exclusion of this arm (#24614) is honoured.

**D4 — the flow CEL `current_user` binding is unchanged: RIGHT.** `runUserOf` still builds the `EvalUser` from `id`, `positions` and `organizationId` only; the diff edits its docblock and the scope note, not its body. The new pin in `flow-cel-current-user.test.ts` evaluates `has(current_user.email)` on a context that carries an email and answers no. This is consistent with ruling #19939 Q2 A as the test header records it (id, positions, organization, platform-admin flag; no email, no name), and `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` keeps saying so truthfully.

**D5 — the published surface: RIGHT, with one wording nit.** `AutomationContext.email?: string` lands in `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts` behind the `contracts` entry's `export *`, with TSDoc naming who sets it (run setup, the decider's switch), who reads it (`resolveRunDataContext`, the RLS compiler), what its absence means (policies drop out, narrowing) and that CEL does not bind it. The interface has no index signature, so the member is a real type widening and `runContext.email` is typed. `RunIdentityContext.email?` (and `RunDataContext`, which extends it) is exported by name from the service-automation entry. `FlowUserGrants.email?` is the return type of `FlowUserGrantsResolver`, the parameter of the public `AutomationEngine.setUserGrantsResolver`, so it is on the published face structurally, but `index.ts` does not re-export the name; the changeset's "Published types" sentence slightly overstates that one. All three members are optional and additive; a host resolver that returns no email still type-checks. `packages/spec/api-surface/contracts.json` records `AutomationContext (interface)` by existence only, so no generated artefact moves, as the dev's `check:generated` reading and the head's Type Check lanes agree.

**D6 — the seeding rule and its fail-safe: RIGHT.** Only a missing fact is resolved; carried positions and permission sets are never re-broadened (the ADR-0090 agent-ceiling case keeps its narrowing). A resolver that answers no email seeds none (`if (needsEmail && grants.email)`), pinned as "never a made-up one". A resolver failure keeps the `warn` level with the same fail-safe argument, and the message now names which facts were lost; the `lost` list is empty-safe. The one cost the rule adds — a context carrying permissions and a peer list but no email asks the resolver once for the email alone (a `subflow` / `map` child of an email-less user, or an in-process caller) — is bounded and declared in the acceptance notes. A `runAs:'user'` run's persisted `context_json` now carries its user's email beside the positions it already carried; that row's read is gated by `sys_automation_run`'s own permissions. Accepted.

**D7 — tests, pins and the head's gates: RIGHT.** The real-stack pin sits beside `runas-user-hook-org-peers.integration.test.ts` as the card asks (its docblock names `runas-user-org-peers.integration.test.ts` as its twin; both files exist). The changed pins are additive except the retitled `crud-runas` fixture (deviation 2, by design). The check-runs on the head are the gate verdicts, read after the last of the 41 completed: the five required contexts — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (with all six shards), `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` — concluded `success`; the Type Check lanes that carry the spec artefact gates (`workspace`, `source gates`, `consumer gates`, `debt ledger`) and every Lint lane concluded `success`; `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Documentation Links`, the docs-affected flag and the four claim / single-writer / part-of guards concluded `success`; the remaining runs (`Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, the dogfood matrix shard job, `Temporal Conformance`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke`) are `skipped`, the full-battery jobs a PR run does not carry. No run is red and none is unfinished.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/24613-run-identity-email.md` grades `@objectstack/service-automation: minor` and `@objectstack/spec: minor`, and its body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`; the PR body carries the same line. That matches what the diff publishes: three optional members added, nothing removed or renamed, no authorable metadata key (`AutomationContext` is a runtime contract interface, not a metadata schema, so no ADR-0087 disposition, tombstone or liveness row is owed), no `skip-changeset`. `yes` takes at least `minor`; `(widening)` is the right arm. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. RIGHT. The one note is D5's wording nit on `FlowUserGrants`; it changes no grade.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each read against the diff:
1. No narrowing, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — consistent with the diff (②).
2. The `crud-runas` fixture retitled and given an email — read; the old shape (permissions and peers, no email) is now pinned separately as "resolves the email alone, and keeps the rest verbatim". Accepted.
3. Two ablations where the dispatch named one — reported with their red counts; cited, not re-run (read-only).
4. The record-change envelope hand-built in the pin because `@objectstack/trigger-record-change` depends on this package — verified: the trigger package's envelope is `record`, `previous`, `object`, `event`, `userId`, optional `tenantId`, `params`, and the pin's `recordChangeEnvelope` matches that shape. Accepted.
5. The before-leg refusal is the by-id not-found rather than the card's record-level sentence — both refuse the row the member can read with their own request. Accepted.
6. The spec suite ran before the merge — the net diff's only `packages/spec` path is the contract file and the merge moved no spec file; `Test Core` on the head covers it. Accepted.
7. The dev stopped its own first spec run (its own process group) — its own PID, process discipline kept. Noted.
8. Commit trailers and the PR footer follow AGENTS.md's model-free form — correct; AGENTS.md takes precedence.

Open question (the flow CEL `current_user` and `email`): the seat's ACCEPT answers A, keep it unbound under ruling #19939 Q2 A. This PR's diff is consistent with A — `runUserOf` is unchanged, the new pin holds `has(current_user.email)` false even when the run context carries one, and the docblocks and `flows.mdx` still state the four-member list. Options B and C would be a re-ruling of Q2 A and are the maintainer's call, not this PR's.

Out-of-scope findings:
- (a) The hook-side twin: `ScopedContext[SEED_USER_GRANTS]` in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` seeds `positions`, `permissions` and `org_user_ids` and not `grants.email` — verified by reading; `packages/objectql/**` is excluded by the claim and the diff does not touch it. Escalated to the seat for the `domain:engine` lane as the card's optional third bullet; not a condition on this PR.
- (b) No door forwards the request's session email; the run takes the stored one — covered in D1; coincide in practice, divergence never widens. Noted, not filed, as the dev wrote.

Claim exclusions held: the net diff touches nothing under `packages/objectql/**`, `packages/core/**` or `packages/plugins/plugin-security/**`, and `resolveRunDataContext`'s system arm is byte-identical (#24614 stays serialised behind this card). Governed surfaces: none in the file list; same-repo head; `size/l`. The docs-drift comment names `flows.mdx` and `actions.mdx` through the `AutomationContext` symbol; neither enumerates the interface's members, and the one sentence about the run carrying no email is about CEL `current_user`, which stays true — no doc edit is owed by this PR.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24613-run-identity-email`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · `domain:services` seat 1 (#6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH` · 2026-10-19T19:32Z · head `5318e58101`.

The contract review of record is PASS `6275514585` at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head. It covers the `contracts/**` widening and every file that hunk makes a claim about. This seat review records the rest. The PR lands through the merge queue.

- **Shape:**
  - The first line is `Fixes #24613`, and that is the only closing keyword in the body.
  - `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is at a line start in the body and in `.changeset/24613-run-identity-email.md`. It covers three optional members: `AutomationContext.email` (`@objectstack/spec/contracts`), `RunIdentityContext.email`, and `FlowUserGrants.email`, which is published only structurally, through `setUserGrantsResolver` (the review's D5 nit).
  - The changeset is `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/service-automation`. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed: this is a runtime contract interface, not an authorable key.
  - Card and PR assignee: `marchtian`.
  - Not governed: `check-governed-merges` reads none of the 9 paths, and 568 changed lines is ≤ 3000.
- **The card's acceptance and triage's shape (`6272563947`), met** (the review's D1–D7):
  - A `runAs:'user'` run carries its user's email. The email is the stored one from `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, or a carried one kept verbatim, and no public door can set someone else's.
  - A `current_user.email` policy now admits the run on the rows it admits for that user's own request, and on nothing beyond. A row assigned to another email is still refused.
  - The decider's segment (PR #24527's path) drops the submitter's email on both postures and seeds the decider's. The dev's second ablation measured the leak this prevents.
  - The `runAs:'system'` arm is byte-identical. The safety plugin does not backfill.
  - The real-stack pin of the card's reproduction sits beside `runas-user-hook-org-peers.integration.test.ts`. Before the fix: 3 failed, 5 passed. After: 8 passed.
- **The dev's open question, answered by this seat: A, keep the flow CEL `current_user` unbound to `email`.** This is ruling #19939 Q2 A as it stands, and this PR's diff is consistent with it: `runUserOf` is unchanged, and the new pin holds `has(current_user.email)` false. No flow in `examples/` or `packages/*/src` reads `current_user.email` in CEL, so there is no pull. Binding it on `runAs:'user'` runs only would give `current_user` a different shape per posture. Executing a standing ruling is not escalated. Re-ruling Q2 A would be the maintainer's act.
- **Gates on this head:**
  - 35 checks succeeded and 6 were skipped by design, the roster set. No check failed, and the five required contexts are green.
  - Locally the dev derived 90 families on this head, ran all 90 and all exited 0 (`--ran`: 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN).
  - Two ablations, each red as predicted, each restored with `git diff HEAD` empty.
- **Spec-lane declaration:** `6274926251` on #18549, before the queue.
- **Accepted deviations:**
  - The `crud-runas` fixture is retitled and carries an email.
  - The record-change envelope is hand-built in the pin, because the trigger package depends on this one.
  - The before-leg's refusal text is the by-id not-found answer.
  - The spec suite ran before the merge; the merge moved no spec file.
  - Two ablations were run where one was asked.
- **Out of scope, one line each:**
  - The hook-side twin (`ScopedContext[SEED_USER_GRANTS]` in `packages/objectql` seeds no email; measured by the dev's probe): filed #24639 (`finding`, for the `domain:engine` lane).
  - No door forwards a session email, and the run takes the stored one. In practice they are the same, and a divergence only narrows. Acceptance notes.
  - #24614 (`resolveRunDataContext`'s system arm) is serialised behind this card (note on #24614).
